findings.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Alphabet reported revenue of $127.577 billion, up 25% from $102.346 billion, operating income of $40.576 billion, up 30%, and an operating margin of 31.8%.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

findings.claim: Google Cloud revenue was $30.709 billion versus $15.157 billion and Cloud operating income was $11.121 billion versus $3.594 billion; remaining performance obligations were $567.7 billion, of which $560.8 billion was Google Cloud, with just over 55% expected to be recognized over the next 24 months.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Google Search & other revenue grew 12% to $63.350 billion, the company said the year-over-year Search query growth rate was the highest in five years, first-party model APIs were processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, the Gemini app reached one billion users, and YouTube Music and Premium surpassed 150 million subscribers including trials.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

findings.claim: YouTube ads were $11.207 billion versus $10.261 billion and Google Network revenue was $7.455 billion versus $7.354 billion, both much slower than the 25% increase in consolidated revenue.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

findings.claim: Net income available to common stockholders fell to $26.170 billion from $34.979 billion and diluted EPS fell to $2.12 from $2.87; the company said a net loss on equity securities of $8.7 billion reduced diluted EPS by $0.55.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

findings.claim: Purchases of property and equipment were $51.355 billion in the third quarter and $131.953 billion for the first nine months of 2026, versus $23.953 billion and $63.596 billion a year earlier, and non-GAAP free cash flow was negative $9.065 billion in the quarter even though trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $19.747 billion.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

findings.claim: Long-term debt was $125.102 billion at September 30, 2026 versus $46.547 billion at December 31, 2025, and Alphabet issued senior unsecured notes for net proceeds of $28.7 billion in the third quarter of 2026.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On November 5, 2026, Alphabet closed an underwritten offering of €6 billion of euro-denominated senior notes, consisting of €750 million floating-rate notes due 2028, €750 million of 3.700% notes due 2028, €1.25 billion of 4.050% notes due 2030, €750 million of 4.250% notes due 2032, €750 million of 4.500% notes due 2035, €750 million of 4.875% notes due 2039, and €1 billion of 5.250% notes due 2045.

On November 24, 2026, Alphabet closed an underwritten offering of C$6 billion of Canadian-dollar senior notes: C$2 billion of 4.100% notes due 2029, C$1.25 billion of 4.800% notes due 2034, C$1.5 billion of 5.325% notes due 2038, and C$1.25 billion of 6.000% notes due 2066.

On June 4, 2026, Alphabet completed a public offering of 29 million Class A shares at $355.1982 and 29 million Class C shares at $351.8018 for net proceeds of $20.5 billion, plus a private placement of 14 million Class A and 14 million Class C shares to a Berkshire Hathaway affiliate for net proceeds of $10.0 billion, and on June 5, 2026 it issued 385 million depositary shares representing 19 million shares of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred stock for net proceeds of $19.0 billion, with mandatory conversion on or about May 15, 2029.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Under a June 1, 2026 at-the-market program of up to $40.0 billion, Alphabet issued 12 million Class A shares for net proceeds of $4.3 billion and 24 million Class C shares for net proceeds of $8.1 billion during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, leaving $27.6 billion available, while the nine-month cash-flow statement shows zero stock repurchases in the first nine months of 2026 and $69.5 billion remained on the April 2025 repurchase authorization.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In July 2026 the European Commission issued Digital Markets Act non-compliance decisions fining Google €430 million for Google Play and €460 million for Search; Alphabet appealed in October 2026 and recognized a $1.0 billion charge in the third quarter of 2026.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: A December 2025 final judgment in the U.S. Search antitrust case restricts how Google distributes its services and requires it to share certain search data and offer syndication to certain competitors; Alphabet appealed in January 2026, the DOJ and states appealed in February 2026, and the appeals were still pending.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In September 2026 the Eastern District of Virginia denied the DOJ's request to divest Google advertising-technology assets and instead ordered behavioral remedies on interoperability, data access, and auction conduct; Alphabet said it plans to appeal the adverse portion of the April 2025 liability decision and may appeal aspects of the remedies decision.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The European Court of Justice denied Alphabet's Android antitrust appeal in July 2026 and Alphabet paid $5.2 billion in cash for the fine plus interest, and in July 2026 a Stockholm court awarded PriceRunner about $2.1 billion, which Alphabet recognized in the second quarter of 2026 and appealed.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: As of September 30, 2026, material purchase commitments were $924.4 billion, of which $802.1 billion was multi-year technical infrastructure, inventory, energy take-or-pay, and content licenses and $213.4 billion was due within 12 months; leases not yet commenced were another $130.5 billion, and contingent data-center backstop obligations were $75.7 billion.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On March 11, 2026, Alphabet completed the acquisition of Wiz for $29.5 billion after purchase-price adjustments and excluding post-combination compensation, and the results are included in Google Cloud.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Other Bets operating loss widened to $2.047 billion from $1.426 billion, and in October 2026 Waymo borrowed $5.0 billion on a senior secured term loan maturing in October 2032 at Term SOFR plus 5.25% that Alphabet does not guarantee.
findings.source_title: Alphabet Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Quarterly cash dividend of $0.22 per share on Class A, Class B, and Class C stock, payable to holders of record on December 7, 2026
Appeals of the December 2025 U.S. Search antitrust final judgment, filed by Alphabet in January 2026 and by the DOJ and states in February 2026, remained pending with no decision date disclosed

policy_links.policy: Digital Markets Act non-compliance decisions on Google Play and Google Search
policy_links.bottleneck: Search and Google Play product-design and billing obligations
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The decisions impose fines and require changes to Search and Google Play; the 10-Q records a $1.0 billion charge and does not tie the decisions to an order or a revenue amount.

policy_links.policy: U.S. District Court final judgment on Google Search distribution and search-data syndication
policy_links.bottleneck: default distribution agreements and competitor access to search data
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The judgment restricts how Google distributes Search and requires data sharing and syndication to certain competitors; the 10-Q does not quantify a revenue effect and appeals are pending.

key_risks.risk: A $40 billion at-the-market program still had $27.6 billion available after third-quarter sales, the 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred converts into common stock by about May 15, 2029, and the cash-flow statement shows no share repurchases in the first nine months of 2026.

Material purchase commitments were $924.4 billion at September 30, 2026, including $213.4 billion due within 12 months, leases not yet commenced were $130.5 billion, and contingent data-center backstops were $75.7 billion.
The December 2025 Search antitrust judgment requires distribution limits, search-data sharing, and syndication, and both sides' 2026 appeals were still pending.

dilution_events_last_12m.description: Public offering of 29 million Class A shares at $355.1982 and 29 million Class C shares at $351.8018, net proceeds $20.5 billion, for general corporate purposes including AI infrastructure.
Private placement of 14 million Class A and 14 million Class C shares to a Berkshire Hathaway affiliate, net proceeds $10.0 billion.
385 million depositary shares representing 19 million shares of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred stock, net proceeds $19.0 billion, mandatory conversion on or about May 15, 2029.

At-the-market sales during the quarter ended September 30, 2026 of 12 million Class A shares for net proceeds of $4.3 billion and 24 million Class C shares for net proceeds of $8.1 billion; $27.6 billion of the $40 billion program remained available. The 10-Q says ATM proceeds are primarily intended to meet tax obligations on employee equity grants.

notes: No going-concern paragraph, delisting notice, or material-weakness disclosure was found. The 10-Q says there were no changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter that materially affected, or were reasonably likely to materially affect, ICFR. The 10-Q is signed October 28, 2026. The November 5 euro notes and November 24 Canadian-dollar notes closed after the September 30 balance sheet, so they are not included in the $125.102 billion long-term debt figure. The November 15, 2026 preferred dividend has passed. A date for the fourth-quarter 2026 earnings release was not found. Short-term accrued legal and regulatory fines and settlements were $13.8 billion at September 30, 2026. Maximum potential payments under TPU repurchase contracts were $6.6 billion, and Alphabet said that fair value was not material. The September 2025 European Commission advertising-technology fine of €3.0 billion predates this 12-month window; the appeal was still pending and is not repeated here as a new event.
